analysis.description: The paper introduces a novel approach to integrating attention mechanisms from Transformer architectures into Neural Cellular Automata (NCA), resulting in a new class of attention-based NCAs termed Vision Transformer Cellular Automata (ViTCA). The study presents both quantitative and qualitative experiments comparing ViTCA to U-Net, a U-Net-based CA baseline, and Vision Transformer on denoising autoencoding tasks across six benchmark datasets, showing ViTCA's superior performance. An ablation study and analysis of ViTCA's architecture, cell state effects, and inductive biases are conducted, demonstrating its enhanced capabilities in various tasks.

name.quote: ViTs leverage the self-attention mechanisms of original Transformers [41], which have emerged as the dominant approach for sequence modelling in recent years. Our work combines foundational ideas from Transformers and ViTs, leading to a new class of NCAs: Vision Transformer Cellular Automata (ViTCA).
